ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

2. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. where is the library

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. happiness

4. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

5. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

6. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

7. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. goes

8. When practising Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

9. When practising Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

10. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

11. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 12.4.1 Guided Composition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

2. A — Where is the library?

3. C — run

4. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

7. A — went

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

12. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 12.4.1 Guided Composition; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
